name: Mariposa · Yosemite
tagline: A historic base for granite country
summary: Use Mariposa as a Yosemite gateway with small-town history between park days. The drive to Yosemite Valley takes time, so in-park accommodation can be worth considering for dawn starts.
seasonNote: Waterfalls are strongest around snowmelt; some high roads close seasonally. Wildfire smoke, snow and roadworks can change access.
arrival: Arrive via FAT, SFO or another California airport, then drive or use scheduled regional transport.
gettingAround: A car offers flexibility; check YARTS and Valley shuttle schedules. Yosemite roads and parking can be congested.
cashTip: Cards are widely used; download plans before weak-signal areas. Budget excludes car/fuel and park fees. 2026 park rule: eligible non-US visitors aged 16+ pay an additional USD 100 at designated parks unless covered by a valid qualifying pass. The nonresident annual pass is USD 250. Verify party coverage; never assume USD 35 covers all visitors.
foodTip: Bring a picnic and reusable water bottle; park food has limited locations and queues.
buyTip: Choose local art or museum gifts; never remove rocks, plants or historical objects.
baseArea: Mariposa for town services; Yosemite Valley for minimum daily driving.

connections.note: Indicative route when seasonal roads allow; winter routes can be much longer. Verify Tioga Road rather than relying on map defaults.

sources.title: Visit California: Wawona and giant sequoias

reviewSummary: Visitor material supports the giant sequoias and Yosemite scenery as the main draw, while Mariposa’s museums provide a slower town day. General entrance reservations are not required in 2026; specific permits still apply.

dayClusters.label: Historic Mariposa and park preparation
dayClusters.note: Use town time for the history museum, local shops and supplies before the longer Yosemite drives. Confirm small-business opening hours; buy early-start food the evening before.

dayClusters.label: Yosemite Valley with Tunnel View
dayClusters.note: Make Tunnel View a short stop on the route into or out of the Valley, not a separate day. Allow the gateway drive and parking/shuttles; shorten the Valley walking plan to match daylight and energy.

dayClusters.label: Glacier Point road day
dayClusters.note: This high-road excursion is conditional on the road being open. Allow the long drive and check current access; use the day as a weather/rest buffer if the road is closed.

dayClusters.label: The southern giant-sequoia grove
dayClusters.note: Make a separate South Entrance/Grove outing and follow current shuttle access. Mariposa Grove is not located in Mariposa town, and the road journey needs a real buffer.
